Conclusion

The default cleaning_damping_length=0.18 is a very strong cleaning-SCALAR damping
choice. In the dimensionless convention of Mignone/Tzeferacos it is alpha=5.5556,
not alpha=0.18. Matching alpha=0.18 with the existing code requires length=1/0.18
=5.5556, reducing the scalar damping RATE by30.8642. This is not proof of a coding
typo: the parameter is explicitly named a length factor, for which the current
formula is internally consistent. It is, however, incompatible with citing a
universal dimensionless alpha0.18 as its justification. Dedner's original0.18 is
a different, dimensional ratio. Strong scalar damping can inhibit magnetic-
divergence removal; the present large comet divergence makes this a material
numerical sensitivity to test before treating96 as an adequate reference.

Primary definitions: distinguish the three quantities

Dedner et al.2002, JCP175,645-673, DOI10.1006/jcph.2001.6961, Eq44-45,p657,
uses psi_t=-(ch^2/cp^2)psi and its exact exponential. Section4,p657 (PDFpage13)
defines cr=cp^2/ch; section5.1,p661/Fig2 reports cr about0.18 on their peak-Bx
test. cr has units of LENGTH. Assigning0.18 to it depends on coordinate units
and is not a universal mesh-scaled nondimensional recommendation.
Primary PDF: https://www.tp4.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/~sw/papers/JCP2002.6961.pdf

Mignone/Tzeferacos2010, JCP229,2117-2138, DOI10.1016/j.jcp.2009.11.026,
section3.3,Eqs26-27,PDFpage8 defines
  alpha=Delta_h*ch/cp^2, Delta_h=min(Delta_x,Delta_y,Delta_z),
  psi_new=psi_old*exp[-alpha*ch*Delta_t/Delta_h],
  tau=cp^2/ch^2=Delta_h/(alpha*ch).
Their tested useful alpha interval is[0,1], problem dependent. They explicitly
point out the dimensional ambiguity of Dedner's mesh-independent cr choice.
https://arxiv.org/html/0911.3410v1#S3.SS3
https://arxiv.org/pdf/0911.3410

Mignone/Tzeferacos/Bodo2010, JCP229,5896-5920,
DOI10.1016/j.jcp.2010.04.013, Eq9 repeats the same convention (alpha_p). Their
rotated shock-tube tests use alpha_p0.8; this further shows that0.18 is not a
universal optimum. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1001.2832

Author-maintained PLUTO4.2 documentation gives GLM_ALPHA=0.1, rather than0.18,
and cites Eq27 for its split GLM_Source. This supports the RATE convention;
it is historical version-specific evidence, not a claim about every release.
https://plutocode.ph.unito.it/Doxygen/API-Reference_Guide/glm_8h.html
https://plutocode.ph.unito.it/files/userguide.pdf

Frozen implementation and exact conversion

The inspected CPU and FP32 Janhunen+postreject sources use
  q_new=q_old*exp[-Delta_t*ch/(L*h_global)], L=cleaning_damping_length,
  h_global=min(rf[1]-rf[0],rmin*dtheta,rmin*cos(latmax)*dphi).
q is stored as psi/ch and the damping factor has the same rate as psi while ch
is held fixed during the split step. Thus
  lambda=1/tau=ch/(L*h_global), cp^2=L*h_global*ch,
  cr=cp^2/ch=L*h_global, alpha_global=1/L.
Two half-damps give one full-step exponential when considering the source alone;
there is no extra factor2 mistake. Hyperbolic/RK generation lies between them.
The code also removes matching q-energy from extended total energy. Damping
preserves gas internal energy in exact arithmetic; changing L may nevertheless
change FP32 cancellation, q content and later hyperbolic evolution. This audit
does not conflate its numerical-energy extension with the paper's full EGLM.

Actual JP96 geometry and local scale

The completed case is96x32x96,uniform r=.0999850461..2.3AU,latitude+-60deg.
  radial width                        0.02291682244AU
  inner theta arc                     0.00654400597AU
  inner latitude-edge phi arc          0.00327200298AU
  h_global                            0.00327200298AU
The minimum is fixed by azimuthal spacing at the INNER radial shell and the
LATITUDE EDGE; it is reused everywhere. This is not the minimum local width
near the comet. At actual day34,r=1.899347565AU,latitude=-6.4934deg:
  local radial width                  0.02291682244AU =7.00391*h_global
  local theta/phi arcs                0.1243120/0.1235145AU
  cube-root cell volume               0.07062268903AU

For default L0.18:
  tau*ch=0.00058896054AU,
  effective local radial alpha=hrad/(L*h_global)=38.9106.
Compared with a LOCAL-radial-length alpha0.18 formula, the damping rate is
216.170times larger. This factor is30.8642 from the reciprocal convention times
7.00391 from the global/local length difference. These are distinct effects.
Changing only L to5.5556 still uses global hmin: effective local radial alpha
is1.26070, not0.18. Matching a local-cell formula would require a separate spatial
coefficient design; it is not silently achieved by taking the reciprocal.
Neither cited uniform-grid paper proves that local-cell damping is the optimal
choice for this spherical wind. Do not combine that change with the first scan.

Configuration-only comparison already selected by root

                    existing          intermediate        alpha0.18 comparator
L                   0.18              1                   5.5555555556
alpha_global        5.5555556         1                   0.18
tau*ch[AU]          0.0005889605      0.0032720030        0.0181777943
local radial alpha  38.910625         7.0039125           1.2607042

These are the smallest useful controls: same frozen source, global hmin, grid,
physical forcing, boundaries, CFL and ch prescription; change one existing
positive configuration scalar. The two alternatives require no new method.
If only one alternative can be afforded, L5.5556 directly tests the convention
suspected here. L1 distinguishes a broad trend from a single large jump. Root
has launched the paired alternatives; this agent launched none. Do not select
an optimum merely because its comet flux agrees better with the exposure.

Why faster scalar damping can leave MORE divB

For the frozen-coefficient, no-flow GLM cleaning subsystem, e=divB and q obey
  e_t=-ch*Laplacian(q), q_t=-ch*e-lambda*q,
so a Fourier mode has
  s_plus/minus=-lambda/2 +/-sqrt((lambda/2)^2-ch^2*k^2).
This is our analytic deduction from the cleaning equations. When lambda>>ch*k,
one branch decays quickly, but the divergence-carrying slow mode has
  s_slow approximately -ch^2*k^2/lambda=-cp^2*k^2.
